AUDIO TRANSCRIPT
ERA II
Dr. Elias Thorne
Vey asked whether PT-9 could explain the chamber gasket failures. Technically, yes. But I'd caution against dramatizing it. PT-9 has always demonstrated limited polymer degradation.
It was useful: a bacterium able to metabolize traces of synthetic material survives when conventional nutrient pathways are interrupted. Under laboratory conditions the degradation rate is slow.

A colony does not eat through a containment wall overnight. Replace the gasket. Change the formulation. Increase inspections. This is a maintenance problem, not evidence of some impossible escape mechanism.
We've discovered bacteria can damage rubber. Civilization has survived worse.

AUDIO TRANSCRIPT
ERA III
Dr. Elias Thorne
I listened to the previous recording. I was wrong. Not about the rate. About the system. PT-9 does not need to consume a containment barrier. It only needs to weaken it.
Microscopic fractures. Damaged membranes. Compromised gaskets. Filters altered enough that the specification is no longer true. Then EP-7 does the rest. The fungus carries the bacteria.
The bacteria creates access for the fungus. We treated two hazards as though they could be added together. They cannot. The relationship multiplies them.
Gloves. Respirators. Electrical insulation. Door seals. Sample bags. Protective coatings. Filters. The containment equipment itself is biologically useful material.
We keep asking how it escaped the barrier. I'm beginning to think that's the wrong question.
